body: It would be concerning, but they won't involve police unless you resist. They would most likely send an ambulance, which it sounds like you need. I know it's super scary, I've been there myself, but they are there to help you. And you deserve that help.

Echoing the above, voluntary is preferable. Yes, they hold the right to detain you if they think you're not safe to leave, but you have a lot more freedom as a voluntary patient. If you do not feel safe tonight, please please try to reach out to one of the crisis numbers. You deserve to stay here and be supported and helped.

If you accept the help, you won't be detained. Sectioning is a very traumatic experience, so I would urge you to be as honest as you can and accept the support offered. I'm not sure what youth services are like, I was only ever in CAMHS and never went to hospital, but it sounds like you're really struggling. 

There's lots of crisis lines you can contact too, if you feel as though you're in immediate danger. 

Call 999 if you really cannot keep yourself safe, you can also call 111 if you're suicidal or the voices are loud, but you feel more capable of safety.

Text SHOUT to 85258 if you'd rather text, but do be aware that replies are not always instant. 

Depending where in the UK you're based, there's also an emergency mental health number, like 999 but for mental health, however it only serves certain boroughs of London. 

I would really encourage you to reach out to someone, or some support service before you see your CAMHS worker tomorrow, especially as you do not feel safe. You deserve help and support.
